newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Wary Australian stocks step higher at open.
newsitem.headline: Wary Australian stocks step higher at open.

text.p: The Australian share market stepped tentatively higher at the opening on Monday after Wall Street steadied but traders remained cautious.
The All Ordinaries index added 10.3 points to 2,433.5.
While the start had been a positive one, brokers said many investors remained wary and gains by the end of the day were likely to be modest.
"It's not going to run ahead of itself today," said a Sydney broker.
"Most are going to wait and see what happens in the U.S. over the next few days."
Global mining giant RTZ-CRA weighed on the market early, down 32 cents to A$18.60 (US$14.69) after going ex-dividend 44.4 cents.

The banks bounced back strongest with the big four all posting solid early gains. ANZ Bank and Westpac Banking Corporation, both up about 1.1 percent to A$7.78 and A$7.12 respectively, were the best performers.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about nine to four, while about 39 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
